The total number of skin conditions was recorded for each participant, and the mean number of skin conditions was calculated. Point prevalence of skin diseases was defined as the proportion of participants with a dermatologist-confirmed diagnosis of any listed condition at the time of the survey. Sampling weights derived from the study sampling framework and the 2020 National Population Census were applied when calculating prevalence and conducting logistic regression analyses. The absolute number of dermatological cases nationwide was estimated by applying prevalence estimates to the 2020 Chinese census data. FINDINGS: From July 1, 2022, to June 27, 2024, 153 593 participants completed the survey and were included in the analysis. The study population had a mean age of 48·5 years (SD 16·8), with 75 512 (49·2%) men and 78 081 (50·8%) women; 98 926 (64·4%) participants resided in urban areas. The age-standardised prevalence of skin diseases was 55·6% (95% CI 51·2-59·9), corresponding to an estimated 618 million (95% CI 567-666) affected adults in China, with a mean of 0·98 (SD 1·22) skin diseases per person. Prevalence increased with age, from 42·0% (95% CI 35·3-48·6) in those aged 18-29 years to 79·5% (75·8-83·1) in those aged 80 years or older (p<0·0001 for trend). Skin diseases were more common in women (56·5%, 51·8-61·1) than in men (54·6%, 50·5-58·7; p=0·023) and more prevalent in southern China (62·5%, 56·2-68·9) than in northern China (47·4%, 43·2-51·7; p<0·0001). Benign cutaneous tumours were the most prevalent type of condition (31·1%, 28·7-33·5), followed by superficial fungal infections (15·0%, 12·5-17·5); dermatitis, eczema, and allergic dermatoses (9·0%, 7·8-10·1); pigmentary dermatoses (7·9%, 6·3-9·6); and sebaceous and sweat gland dermatoses (5·7%, 5·0-6·4). Factors associated with skin diseases included female sex, increasing age, residence in southern China, current or former smoking, current or former alcohol consumption, overweight or obesity, a history of allergies, and a history of photosensitivity. Despite the substantial burden, only 5·8% (4·5-7·3) of affected individuals had sought medical care, and 18·2% (16·7-19·9) had used over-the-counter medications in the past year. INTERPRETATION: Skin diseases could affect more than half of Chinese adults. These findings highlight a substantial unmet need and should inform national priorities. FUNDING: National Key R&D Program of China, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, National Natural Science Foundation of China, and Non-profit Central Research Institute Fund of Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences.

title: Trends in the burden of diseases and their associations with multidimensional development among children and adolescents in China from 2000 to 2019: a retrospective analysis of a nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional survey
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid social progress has transformed the health profile of Chinese children and adolescents, with declining diseases associated with poverty and rising diseases associated with wealth. This study aims to describe national trends in disease transitions and examine their associations with multidimensional provincial development. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analysed data from the 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019 waves of the nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional Chinese National Surveys on Students' Constitution and Health in Han Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years from 30 provinces in mainland China. The survey used a multistage, stratified, cluster-sampling design with balanced distributions by age, sex, and residence (urban vs rural). Collected data were prevalences of diseases associated with wealth and development (overweight and obesity, dental caries, and visual impairment) and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with wealth) in addition to diseases associated with poverty (undernutrition, anaemia, and Ascaris infestation), and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with poverty). We integrated 13 provincial indicators reflecting economic, social, environmental, infrastructure, and innovation development to construct a Multidimensional Equality Development Index (MEDI) using an entropy method. To examine national trends in disease transitions and their associations with multidimensional development we used mixed-effects logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Population-attributable fractions were estimated to describe how development domains related to disease patterns. FINDINGS: The study included 1 085 072 participants across five survey waves. Between 2000 and 2019, nationally, the prevalence of diseases associated with wealth increased and that of diseases associated with poverty declined substantially. In 2019, prevalence of visual impairment was highest (67·8%), followed by overweight and obesity (24·3%), dental caries (21·9%), multimorbidity associated with wealth (20·1%), anaemia (10·1%), undernutrition (4·7%), Ascaris infestation (0·8%), and multimorbidity associated with poverty (0·5%). The overall median MEDI score increased from 0·11 (IQR 0·09-0·16) in 2000 to 0·20 (0·15-0·28) in 2019. When data were pooled over 20 years, restricted cubic-spline analyses showed a non-linear association between MEDI score and odds of the disease outcome; higher MEDI scores were generally associated with lower odds of diseases associated with poverty, and higher odds of diseases associated with wealth (excluding visual impairment). INTERPRETATION: Multidimensional development was associated with simultaneous reductions in prevalence of diseases associated with poverty and increases in prevalence of diseases associated with wealth. Disparities in most diseases associated with wealth between higher and lower MEDI areas have largely narrowed, suggesting a potential dual burden in lower MEDI areas and the need for targeted strategies. These findings highlight the need to enhance cross-sector investments to promote balanced, sustainable improvements in child and adolescent health. FUNDING: The National Key Research and Development Programme of China and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
